hints: Focus on two separate tests here, first whether the OH carbon is secondary, then what size alkene it would make.
Remember a secondary alcohol has the OH carbon joined to two other carbons, so check each structure for that pattern first.
Work out what Mr = 70 means for an alkene using 12n + 2n - 2, then see which secondary alcohol has that same carbon skeleton.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a secondary alcohol**

A secondary alcohol has the C-OH carbon bonded to two other carbon atoms and one H. A tertiary alcohol has it bonded to three carbons, a primary to only one.

Rule: $1^\circ$: $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$, $2^\circ$: $\text{R}_2\text{CHOH}$, $3^\circ$: $\text{R}_3\text{COH}$

**Classify A to D**

Look carefully at the carbon bearing OH. A is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$, tertiary. B is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3$, secondary. C is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, secondary. D is cyclopentanol, secondary.

So A is eliminated, B, C and D remain.

**Find the formula of an alkene with Mr = 70**

General formula for an acyclic alkene is $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$. So Mr is:
$$M_r = 12n + 2n = 14n = 70$$
$$n = 5$$
So we need a 5-carbon acyclic alkene, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$. This must come from a 5-carbon alcohol by loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

**Match the carbon count**

B is a $\text{C}_5$ alcohol (3-methylbutan-2-ol) so dehydration gives $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$, Mr = 70. C is only $\text{C}_4$ (butan-2-ol) so gives $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$, Mr = 56. D is $\text{C}_5$ but cyclic, so gives cyclopentene $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8$, Mr = 68.

Only the secondary $\text{C}_5$ acyclic alcohol fits both conditions.

options.A: This is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol because the OH carbon is joined to three other carbons. Although dehydration would give a C5 alkene with Mr = 70, it fails the first test of being secondary.
options.B: This is 3-methylbutan-2-ol. The OH carbon is joined to two carbons, so it is secondary. It has 5 carbons, so dehydration by loss of H2O gives C5H10 with Mr = 5x12 + 10 = 70. It passes both tests.
options.C: This is butan-2-ol, which is indeed secondary, but it has only 4 carbons. Its dehydration product is butene, C4H8 with Mr = 56, not 70. This traps students who check alcohol class but forget to check Mr.
options.D: Cyclopentanol is secondary, but dehydration gives cyclopentene, C5H8. Because the ring already removes two H atoms, Mr = 60 + 8 = 68, not 70. This traps students who assume any C5 alcohol gives Mr = 70.
